limitations: Seven fixed synthetic release workloads are local timing diagnostics. The 64-point case is slower; the first allocation variant and every sample remain retained. Neither wall-clock ratios nor synthetic geometry qualify vehicle sensing accuracy, whole-stack performance or real-time deadlines.

The 48 preceding authored recordings contain no cloud above 64 retained points. They certify the small-cloud pipeline path. The added dense stop supplies actual >64-point acquisition coverage in both plants, preserving parent physical outcomes and raw/replay bytes. It is an additional viewed condition, not a replacement for old mission failures.

The original directed algorithm is order-dependent. Equivalence concerns the same input order; it does not establish permutation invariance, improved shape confidence, association identity or new forecast calibration.

The index uses extra linear storage; small clouds and extreme finite coordinate domains retain exhaustive scanning. Deterministic work bounds apply to the specified test layouts, not arbitrary worst-case latency.

No new driving-availability gain, measured automotive data, real-vehicle safety, remote CI execution or cross-platform success is claimed. All eight original incomplete missions and the 30 percent waypoint remain open.
